questions.q: In C99 and later, what is the output of the following code?
questions.e: Since C99, integer division truncates towards zero, so -7 / 3 is -2 and the remainder -7 - (-2 × 3) = -1. The remainder takes the sign of the dividend.

questions.q: Which format specifier is used with printf to print an unsigned decimal integer?
questions.e: %u prints an unsigned int in decimal. %i is the signed integer, %f is for floating point, and %s is for strings.

questions.q: If no storage class is mentioned, a local variable declared inside a function in C belongs to the ______ storage class.
questions.e: Local variables are automatic by default. They are created on entry to the block and destroyed on exit, and they hold garbage unless initialised.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about opening files with `fopen` in C.
I. Mode "a" creates the file if it does not exist, and all writes go to the end of the file.
II. Mode "w" on an existing file keeps its old contents and adds new data after them.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: I is true. II is false: mode "w" truncates an existing file to zero length, so the old contents are lost. Only "a" keeps the contents and appends.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a keyword in C?
questions.e: C has no built-in string type: strings are arrays of char. typedef, register and volatile are all C keywords.

questions.e: The additive operator + has higher precedence than the shift operator <<, so the expression is 1 << 3, which is 8.

questions.q: What is the output of the following C code? (char is 8 bits)
questions.e: The sum 260 is converted back into an unsigned char, which is defined to wrap modulo 256. So the result is 260 − 256 = 4.
